However, if this is so, and if it is logical, it is not clear to me why you allow, during the examination-in-chief, for documents to be introduced which have nothing to do with this witness and allow remarks for which on many occasions he has said that he has heard about them from the media but doesn't have any personal knowledge of that. And particularly if it has to do with documents that he has no personal knowledge of. And very many such documents have been admitted, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you can make your objection when we come to specific evidence, and we'll consider it, but there is little point asking a witness, as you have done on occasion, about what he heard on the radio or something of that sort, when there are very general points to be made by you. Now, let's try and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you are familiar with the broader area of Western Slavonia, where the Serb population was left without protection with the withdrawal of the JNA, especially near Okucani and Pakrac and there was this large exodus where tens of thousands of citizens left the area of Slatina and other areas on horse carts and so on. Do you remember that a decision of the government of Yugoslavia and the date is the 3rd of November, 1991, sent a letter to Lord Carrington, as the chairman of the conference, and also Mr. van den Broek, since the Netherlands also was, at that time, chairman of the 12 and he was the president of the council of the economic community, so those areas of Croatia were unprotected because they were at the -- exposed to strikes by the Croat forces. So do you remember that this was information that was forwarded to Lord Carrington and Mr. van den Broek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was something incorrect in your question. The JNA did not withdraw from Western Slavonia to Pakrac, because it was not there in Pakrac, but the Territorial Defence units withdrew together with the population, the JNA was from -- was at Okucani, and up to Stara Gradiska up to Pakrac. So it wasn't in Pakrac. I remember that. The other thing is I do remember such a letter being sent, and I heard that from the media. I was in Western Slavonia and was not in a position to see something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that the army did not advance beyond Pakrac but you don't know anything about the reasons why that was so; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is noted. You say that some group carried out murders in Vucin but you didn't see that personally; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it myself, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you didn't even report anything to anybody regarding this murder in Vocin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not report it to anybody, because when I heard about it, it was already late December, and I reacted on this issue via the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you have no idea whether anybody kept the authorities in Belgrade informed about this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned some units of Vuk Draskovic and other paramilitary formations. You yourself don't know anything about those paramilitary formations; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about those paramilitary organisations, and I did make a correction, and I said that those were not units of Vuk Draskovic; they were ascribed to Seselj. But I don't know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You ascribed them to Seselj, but you don't know whether they were Seselj's or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The citizens thought that they belonged to him, particularly after Seselj came and reviewed his volunteer units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A group of those people whom you claim were his volunteers, you saw them without weapons; is that true? This is what I heard during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The group, when it arrived, I saw a group without weapons, and I saw a group with weapons, and I said that this was near the village of Glavica, and I also stated that during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a group of people, among whom was a person called Rastovic, who exerted pressure on certain groups of people. You mentioned an incident where he threatened you with a pistol, and you also mentioned Milan Babic as belonging to that group of extremists. My question is: Is it true that you never heard that Babic threatened anybody or asked -- or demand that somebody be killed? You never heard him say that; is that so or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard Babic demand that anybody be killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as I understand, you don't have any knowledge, and you don't know anything regarding the distribution of weapons or anything about Martic's involvement in that, even though you testified about Martic as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the distribution of weapons that he carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say Martic had support from Belgrade and that Martic was informed about the crimes. You say that he was informed about the crimes carried out by his police forces and that he did not punish or dismiss anybody. This is what you claim. But you don't have any knowledge either about the alleged crimes which you ascribed to Martic, or about his activities. Is this true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that Martic, who was the chief of police down there, was informed about what was going on and what his men were doing, so I based my conclusion on that. I wasn't next to him, so I was not able to see what he was doing and how he was doing it, but I drew my conclusion based on the fact that he was the chief of police and that he was leading those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirmed my question about Croats who were living normally in Knin and Martic told me about them, that there was no discrimination, that they were able to live normal lives, and you confirmed that. You said yesterday that you knew that Croats who lived there normally and without any pressure whatsoever, they lived there in their own houses; is that so or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that. I know that there were Croats in Knin, that there were many mixed marriages, there were many friends, and I know that they lived there. But I did not say that there were also Croats who were left, and there were such Croats who left. I don't know specifically who but I heard that Croats had left Knin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you don't know about what I just asked you about, how can you know that individuals under the command of Martic carried out crimes and that he knew about that and that he did not wish to punish anyone? Did you inform anybody at any time, anybody in Belgrade, for example, about those crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During 1991, I didn't hear anything. I didn't have the opportunity to do that. It was a long way away. So I just heard about that. And if I had heard about that, I expected that others had heard about that too. So it wasn't up to me to deal with matters like that when there were people there who were responsible for such matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I assume, Mr. May, that you will tell me that some of my questions have to be in closed session, so may we briefly go into closed session so that I will not disrupt your proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back into open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to put only a few questions to you in connection with your examination-in-chief. You were shown the territory, and the question was asked of you as to when this area was put under Serb control, and you said in late 1991. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what map you are referring to and what area, because in late 1991, only the area around Knin, Benkovac, Gradacac, and Lapac was under Serb control, later it expanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your explanation that the Serbs put this area under their control and the very term "control," is it evident that this was an area where the Serbs had lived for at least a few centuries? Is this in dispute or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an area that they had inhabited for several centuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Catholic churches destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Milosevic. Is the map you are referring to the tab 5 of Exhibit 326? Can the witness be shown the map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. To avoid wasting time, the point I wanted to make, Mr. Kwon, was that putting territories under control does not mean that the Serbs occupied somebody else's territory. These were territories they had inhabited for centuries. The map itself doesn't have any major significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put the map on the ELMO. I think that's tab 6, but is this the map you're referring to? Is it right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't thinking of the map itself. I was speaking of the year 1991, but this was brought up because a map was shown to him. He has already answered my question, Mr. Kwon. I don't want to waste any time discussing maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you then whether Catholic churches had been destroyed, whether you know about a Catholic church that was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the one in Okucani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know about one Catholic church. Do you know of any others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of some in Dalmacija, but I don't know the names of the villages, just as I did not keep a record of Serbian churches, I didn't keep a record on Catholic churches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Recently I showed you a list of tens -- of dozens of Orthodox churches that had been destroyed and you said you knew about those, or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I knew about some churches. You asked me about the number, and I said I didn't know the exact number because it was the church that kept these records. I know that some churches were destroyed, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to save time, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked during the examination-in-chief, when you mentioned that meeting, whether any party contacts with the socialist party, did you have any party contacts with my party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the socialist party is a left-wing party and that the Serb Democratic Party, at the elections in Serbia, was an opposition party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what sort of collaboration are you talking about when you talk about collaboration between the Socialist Party and the party you say you know was in the opposition at the elections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the SDS from Croatia. As far as I can recall, Babic and several others said they had contacts. What sort of contacts, I don't know, and whether they actually had them or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the media was under government control. Do you remember that in these same media you claim were under government control, which is not correct, your then minister of foreign affairs wrote an article against me in which he even claimed - I ask you if you remember this - that Cyrus Vance had bribed me with 120 million dollars to accept the arrival of UN troops and to support this in the area where later on the UN zones were established? Do you remember this? This was in the Belgrade press, the Yugoslav press.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what minister you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was Caslav Vocic at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I don't know about this because I didn't know Caslav Vocic. I never met him. I'm not saying it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When speaking of control over the media and, as you say, that the media allegedly worked against the interests of peace, and I say this cannot be linked up with the authorities in Belgrade, but did you say during your examination-in-chief that you only heard about the alleged camps in Knin and Udbina from the Croatian media? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only heard about this from the Croatian media. You know nothing of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said -- or rather, you mentioned a colonel or I'm not sure what his rank was. I think he was a colonel, Celeketic, who as you say, came from Yugoslavia. Where was Colonel Celeketic from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I heard, he was born in Kikinda. He was in the barracks in Bjelovar. In 1991 he came to Okucani. Later on, I don't know where he went, but he turned up again in 1993, in Okucani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was in Bjelovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said a lot about the manner in which things functioned within the Republic of Srpska Krajina. Do you know whether anyone imposed anything on you from outside with respect to your political positions, your behaviour or attitudes, and so on and so forth? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know only that the Association of Serbs in Croatia interfered and radicalised matters against Jovan Raskovic and in favour of Babic. Their pressure was exerted in this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's another matter. That's your internal problem. But as far as I can recall the reactions of Belgrade, can you confirm these were always aimed exclusively, if there were any suggestions or, as you say, pressures, in the direction of accepting a peaceful solution, accepting the Vance plan, Vance-Owen Plan, the arrival of the UN, cooperation with them and opening up dialogue between Zagreb and Knin? Is this true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already spoken of this in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Zagreb Knin dialogue was opened up and that Nikolic and Sardonic negotiated on several occasions, that the main road was opened up, that there was economic cooperation and so on, and that on both sides the governments discussed this, it was written about in the media, Owen and Stoltenberg mediated in this respect, they had a meeting at the Zagreb airport, Pleso airport. Do you know about these activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about these activities. I know there was resistance to them and I know that because of this, the presidents of the municipalities of the Republic of Serbian Krajina went to see you, that you supported the opening up of the motor way and the opening up of a dialogue between Zagreb and the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point you said that the Serbian state security incited people at rallies. Did you say that? Did you say that on the basis of your personal knowledge or did you hear about this from someone else or didn't you -- maybe you didn't say it at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that this was done by the security services of Serbia. What I said was that it was security agents who did this in the field. But what services they actually belonged to, whether they were local ones, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. According to my notes, because your testimony was given a few days ago, you said that refugees from Croatia were sent on to Kosovo. Did you mention that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you find this out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this from some of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From some of the refugees who went to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from some refugees who were in the column but didn't go to Kosovo. They told me that some had been sent to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Kosovo makes up 10 per cent of the territory of Serbia? This is a geographical fact. And are you aware of the fact that only one per cent, that is, ten times below the average, of the refugees went to the area of Kosovo and Metohija within Serbia, which is ten times less than went to other parts of Serbia? Are you aware of this? Only one per cent of these refugees went to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't talking about figures and how many refugees went where in Serbia, nor do I know what percentage of the territories taken up by Kosovo. I only know that they went to the south of Serbia, and I mentioned Kosovo. I didn't say they went exclusively to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You accept, then, the fact that in view of the figures I have put forward, the least amount of refugees went in the direction of Kosovo. Did you mention that Croats were expelled from Serbia? I have a note about this, but I'm not sure what words you actually used. You were referring to Vojvodina primarily.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that. Based on statements made by some Croats who arrived in Western Slavonia and said they had been expelled from their villages. I have no other knowledge apart from this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no knowledge about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Vojvodina, so I didn't see these events. I made my statement on the basis of what I heard from Croats who arrived in Western Slavonia, asking for a place to live, and some of them, as I remember, went to Korenica. And my statement was made on the basis of what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a single example of the torching of someone's house or the looting of the property of any Croat in Serbia or the forcible expulsion of any individual there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for burnings of houses, I didn't hear that, but I have told you what I did hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard this from some Croat who arrived in Western Slavonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that throughout the ten years of the Yugoslav crisis, it is only in Serbia that the ethnic make-up of the population didn't change at all? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the Serbs who escaped, who fled from Western Slavonia were arrested. Were they arrested in Serbia by anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I heard there were such incidents, that they were arrested there and taken to Bosnia. I think I heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I just wanted to know how certain you were of this. You said that some of them were arrested in Eastern Slavonia. Is this correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure they were arrested and mistreated and beaten up and humiliated in Eastern Slavonia, and this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't have any such knowledge about Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not any specific knowledge, but I think I did hear of several people who were arrested and taken to the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were taken to the front in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were arrested and several of those hundreds of thousands who fled, do you have any explanation which should be logical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no personal knowledge about that, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it after the Storm Operation, several months later, when people got together and started talking about those events. I think it was then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these were rumours after the Operation Storm, that is, the ethnic cleansing of Serbs from Croatia and the offensive against Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what I heard after those events. I have no other evidence except what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. C-037, at the time of the attack on the territories inhabited by Serbs, is it disputed that those territories were under the protection of the United Nations, so-called UN-Protected Areas? They were known as UNPA zones, United Nations-Protected Areas. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it then true that all those large-scale attacks, when in Western Slavonia the number were expelled that we have already mentioned, then in the Knin Krajina, and the other 250.000 people, and these numerous crimes, that all these occurred in areas that were under United Nations protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the Serbs agreed to the plan to be placed under United Nations protection and that they were promised to be protected until a political solution was found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they protected until a political solution was found or were they expelled as a result of these crimes committed against them in the presence of the United Nations forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not protected, obviously, when all this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe that a crime was committed against the Serbs with the co-responsibility of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Not a matter for the witness. His opinion about that is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add, the Serbian side also made an omission, a significant one. According to the Vance plan, they should have been demilitarised, which means the heavy weapons should have been placed under UN control and only the police was to be left with weapons. We did that in Western Slavonia, and we were given written guarantees that we would be protected. The rest did not do that. Later on, in the course of 1993 and 1994, weapons were taken and given to people who formed units. When I spoke to the commander in Western Slavonia, General Zabalo, about protection, because people were afraid if they were not protected, that they would get killed. His answer was as follows, and I would like to quote him. I don't know whether that would be the same now, but he said: If both sides have weapons and use them, then the United Nations units will not put themselves in between the two, because they would get killed as a result of conflicts. But if demilitarisation is completed and the weapons placed under control, then the United Nations will take upon itself full responsibility. And this was the omission made by the Krajina authorities, what weapons they had proved to be insufficient, and using them or not using them could not protect the people. I do not in this way relieve Croatia of the responsibility for what it did in this area, especially after the exodus of the population, but I do consider that the political leadership of Krajina is also responsible if it accepted the Vance plan, why didn't it carry it out fully and thereby transfer full responsibility to the international forces, which would have to accept that responsibility. In this way, an excuse or justification, or I don't know what, was given to them, for them to say demilitarisation was not carried out and we cannot place our forces between two armed formations. Whether they were equally well armed or not, I don't know, because I'm not a military expert, but I believe, and I repeat, that I think part of the responsibility is with the people who represented the people -- with the authorities, not the people, exposing the population to the danger and to the events that occurred there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you go on, let's just clarify something. General Zabalo, who you spoke to, was he the UN commander in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. He was the commander of the Sector West up until the end of February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, but let's clear up one point. Since you skipped over some -- or at least one very important detail. First of all, do you remember that according to the Vance plan, which the Serbs accepted, the weapons, true, had to be placed under a double key: One key would be in the hands of the Krajina Serbs and the other in the hands of the UN, and the Serbs did hand over their weapons and they did carry out the demilitarisation and it was only the police that was left with what they called side arms, that is, pistols. Do you remember, therefore, that they did fulfil their obligation but that they took up arms again from those same depots when they were attacked, and not before they were attacked? You should know this, and you probably do have this book, because I don't have time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let the witness answer the point that's made. Just a moment. The point that is made is that the Krajina Serbs in fact complied, but it's said they took up arms when they were attacked. Can you help us as to that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They resorted to tanks and cannon then, but not long barrel weapons, because they were present in the territory of Krajina. And when I was mobilised, I saw that people were carrying rifles, and this was also contrary to the Vance plan. And the best guarantee is if the international forces that are present, that are supervising the area and who are intended to protect the area, that they say that the disarming has been done, and not by certain officials who judge the disarming according to their own criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: C-037, here's a book about the Miljevac Plateau of 1992, are you familiar with that book, which discusses the attack against an area again under UN protection? Are you familiar with this book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the events. I have not seen the book. I know that those people were massacred, even in Croatia. I saw a video recording of those events, the Miljevac Plateau, when a film was made against the crimes against Serbs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have this offensive against UNPAs in 1993, Maslenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of those events too, but I haven't seen that book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have a book on the expulsion of Serbs from Krajina in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that book either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you at least have the book concerning Western Slavonia, May 1995, and the exodus of Serbs from Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I was not given that book either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just tell you that from Western Slavonia and quoting from a letter by Yasushi Akashi, a special envoy of the UN Secretary-General, who says the government of the republic of Croatia should immediately halt the military offensive launched by its forces in the area of Western Slavonia, known as the Sector West, which it started on the 1st of May, 1995, in the morning, in violation of the agreement on the cessation of hostilities of the 29th of March, 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let me get the chronology right. The indictment is dealing with events in 1990 and 1991. What is the relevance of events in 1995? You've been given considerable leeway to go into those events, but I'm concerned that they may have no relevance at all to what happened five years earlier. It may be there was, and I don't take a view. It may be there was an attack at that stage. But is it of any assistance, is it of any relevance at all during the trial?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to establish, Mr. May, that in addition to crimes being committed and a complete ethnic cleansing of Serbs from Croatia, those crimes were committed in a territory and at a time when that territory was under the protection of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's the relevance of that? What is the relevance of that to this trial, what happened in 1990 and 1991? You seem to lose the focus which is necessary in a trial, which is on the particular charges, not on other wrongs that may have been done at some other time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, if you dwell only on the years 1990 and 1991 and 1992, then you will see that what I'm claiming is true, and that is that in those years, the Serbs were defending themselves against a pogrom and that from the moment the United Nations forces arrived, they trusted those forces and expected to be protected until a political settlement was found. They handed over their weapons under double key and they took them back only after the attacks that are described in these books in order to defend themselves, because they were not protected by the United Nations, as they were promised they would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the books are not admissible. They're various opinions. We admit reports and the like, but I doubt those books have any value, although we'll consider them in due course if you want to put them in. Mr. Kay, I don't want to take up time with -- I'm sorry. I don't want to take up time. The accused has another five minutes. But in relation to the events in Kosovo, where, of course, there was a direct relevance of the activities of the KLA and also there was maybe relevance to the NATO bombing, you put in a paper, or the amici put in a paper, concerning the scope of cross-examination. I would find it helpful myself to find a similar paper in relation to events in Croatia, because for the moment I am not convinced of the relevance of events in 1995 to an indictment which is concerned with 1990 and 1991. But if may be you would like to reflect on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will certainly attempt to do that for the Trial Chamber. It may well be here that the accused is dealing with an entire picture that the Prosecution have made against him, asserting that he has been double-dealing, that he didn't keep to promises, and in many respects that the whole period from 1990 up to 1999, as characterised by the way the Prosecution put their case, is something that the accused feels he needs to deal with in this particular way, to demonstrate that he in fact was attempting to abide by international agreements, so far as he could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But to use the argument that because wrongs were done to Serbs in 1995, it justified behaviour in 1991 is one which I will need to be convinced of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The context that I put it in is the picture that the Prosecution have presented to this Trial Chamber in opening their cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not a matter we can debate now, although I opened it up. Time is limited. The accused should have his extra five minutes and then you should be able to cross-examine. But perhaps you can put a paper on it and we'll take it from there. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. You want to add a bit more? I've asked the amici to put a paper in, and when that's in, you can address us on it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You just said that I was trying to explain, by events in 1945, what happened in 1991, which is absolutely incorrect, because the violence --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not true that what happened in 1991 -- 1995 - I'm trying to explain what happened in 1991. On the contrary. I have shown here that the violence against the Serbs started already in 1989, 1990, 1991, and 1992. I've been questioning this witness alone about 1991 and 1992. So it is obvious why the United Nations arrived, because those areas needed to be protected. Did they protect them? They did not. Did the Serbs accept them? They did. So it's not what Mr. Kay says, that only I wanted a peaceful solution. The Serbs in Krajina accepted the United Nations and agreed to a political settlement, by political means. But no political solution was found, and they were expelled. I'm talking about crimes committed in a civil war, provoked by the forcible secession of Croatia from Yugoslavia, against Yugoslavia, and especially against the Serb population. And here an inversion is being made. The victim is proclaimed the culprit, and the victim in that civil war in Croatia was the Serb people living on their own territory, Mr. May. And all the events that I have questioned this witness about refer to 1991 and 1992, and prove precisely what I'm alleging, and I'm just showing the fact that what the Serbs agreed to in those United Nations-Protected Areas was not -- did not lead to a political settlement but rather to an aggression and crimes against them. So it is absolutely impossible to reverse things, to turn things upside down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... cross-examine in relation to any events in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only the last three minutes, Mr. Robinson. I asked him about this, and I wanted to ask whether these areas from which the Serbs were ethnically cleansed, at the time when this was done, were under the protection of the United Nations. And I wanted that to be established, and nothing more than that. And during the two days of cross-examination, I've spent two minutes on 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Five minutes more, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. C-037, is it completely clear that the civil war in Croatia - we were now discussing events in 1990, the amendments of the constitution, the new constitution, the firing of Serbs, the killings, illegal arrests, violence, et cetera, the events that occurred in 1990, 1991, and 1992, that these were provoked by violence on the part of the Croatian state at the time in the process of forcible secession from Yugoslavia, violence against the Serb population, and against the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness -- you asked him that and he's given an answer. Do you want to add anything, Witness C-037, to what you've already said on this topic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing more to add. I have said everything I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are we quite clear on that point, that this was a civil war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter we're going to have to decide. That's a matter -- that's a matter of law which has got to be decided by us. Not for the witness to decide.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you can decide that today is Monday, as far as that is concerned. I was talking here about facts, and all the answers given by the witness confirm the facts that I have presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Two more questions, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. C-037, is it your opinion that the civil war was imposed upon the Serbs in Croatia by the behaviour of the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that it was imposed upon them, but I can say that tension was provoked, mistrust of Serbs towards the authorities in Croatia, and a split, a serious split, between them occurred, but I wouldn't give any other legal attributes to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you, Mr. C-037, believe that when we're talking about Serbs in Croatia in that civil war, was that war for them a defensive war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how the Serbs behaved and that is how they felt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is how they behaved and how they felt. Did you ever hear of any intention on the part of the Serbian Krajina to occupy any part of territory belonging to the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kay. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll deal with one matter first of all and then I'll deal with Judge Kwon's matters, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Was this in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. This was a private for private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Into private session then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we turn to tab 12 and if that could be put before the witness as well. This is a document about which you were asked questions at the beginning of the week, 30th of September, LiveNote 10434. It's a document from the war crimes department, or department for war crimes, and it's a document that lists various events as having taken place on a date in 1991, as well as with a list of names. Are you looking at the B/C/S version at the moment? If you, Witness C-037, if you just look at the B/C/S version rather than the English version. Is it a form of document that you recognise at all in your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw it here at the Prosecutor's office for the first time, such a document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you in a position to state in any way about its production or how it came into being, from any knowledge of your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was compiled by the MUP of Croatia, by interviewing the citizens of Vocin and gathering the information about those events. What I saw later, and which was confirmed, and that was the only thing was by naming people who -- Serbs who had committed crimes against Croats, people were mentioned who -- about there was no proof that they had committed them. So the same applies to this document here, that there are too many names here with unsubstantiated claims. So this happened in the case of Vocin as well, and I had heard this from the Croat media and as well as from Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I need asked about it. Does that help Judge Kwon on the matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour asked me to address you on evidential status about that, but I'm not sure I really need to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dealing with one other aspect of your evidence, C-037, you gave evidence of discriminating laws against the Serbs in Croatia, concerning their national holidays, their education, other aspects of their life. Are you able to give the dates of those discriminating laws that you were talking about, or the approximate dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only give you approximate dates. This was in the course of 1990 and 1991 that such laws were enacted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, on just one other matter: The proposal that the Serbs weren't a constituent people within Croatia, that you said caused a lack of confidence in the new government, was that about the same time period as well, 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you described in the 1990 elections that there were insulting attitudes towards Serbs by Croatian political parties. Could you tell us what you were able to see as the effect that that had on the Serb population within Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was humiliating for the Serbs, it was an irritation, and it also prompted distrust towards the new political authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned during the cross-examination Jovo Vezmar, and you said that he went to Serbia in 1995. Did he go to Serbia at an earlier time as well? When did he go to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say 1995. The first time he went was in 1991. Maybe on the 10th of March or the 7th or 8th of March, and he came back in August, in 1991, and then he left finally again at some point in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he was in Serbia in 1991, did he achieve a post within the MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in the Pancevo police station. I don't know exactly what his job was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the -- in relation to the relation between the TO and the JNA, you said that you would not know about this, and I would like to clarify to which time this relates. When the Banja Luka Corps arrived in Pakrac in September 1991, was the TO Western Slavonia then subordinated to the JNA in this region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, the TO commanders went to Bijela Stijena, where the forward command post of the Banja Luka Corps was, and I think that they were subordinated to the command of the Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they paid, the TO staff? Was it also paid by the Banja Luka Corps at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that after October they did receive a salary. I heard that from regular soldiers, and I also heard that the TO command issued salaries to the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the fear that the Serbs felt given these changes within the constitution and other matters in the society in Croatia. Was that fear fuelled by the SDS politicians, by certain SDS politicians, or Serbian politicians or Serbian media? Would you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by local Serb politicians at the SAO Krajina at that time, tension was raised. So any distrust that appeared amongst the Serbs, they incited it even more at the rallies, they had people with Chetnik insignia who also recalled the ugly past, which was in common with them, and with their shouting, they created fear among the Serbs, as well as the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the state-owned Serbian media play a role in instilling this fear or increasing the fear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When such statements were published or issued by the local politicians, then I think the broadcasting of such statements would increase the tensions that were already there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you saw already in June 1991 people armed. Do you refer to Serbs, Croats, or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, both sides had weapons: Croats and Serbs both. Some had hunting rifles, some had obtained automatic rifles. There were also pump-action rifles. They were -- it was possible to purchase them. So I know that both the Croats and the Serbs were arming themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described many crimes committed against the Serbs, and you said that as early as mid-June -- mid-1991 you heard about such crimes. Those crimes, did they happen before the war broke out or clashes broke out, or during those fights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In mid-1991 this happened, but there were incidents which preceded these conflicts. But I didn't hear anything detailed about such incidents, but I did hear that they did take place in the territory of Eastern Slavonia. Once the war began, there was more talk about such incidents, but now, I don't know if these are authentic stories about these events or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Western Slavonia, those crimes that you described, did they occur after the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding Western Slavonia, I think they took place after the war broke out, that there were incidents, fights, for example, but I know that Serbs in Western Slavonia before the war killed I think three police officers, one at Obrijez and two near Trnakovac, in Okucani. So there were events like this as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they killed three policemen, do you mean Croatian policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were Croatian policemen. They were on duty. They were on their way to work. Two of them were ambushed and killed, and one of them was killed while he was standing on the road near Obrijez, turning to Obrijez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the prison camp in Bucje, you mentioned that besides Croats, also some Serbs were detained there. Why were they detained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These Serbs who were detained were, I would say, the opponents of people who were in the TO command. Perhaps people were jealous. They were well off. I had heard from them while they were arrested they were robbed. Their property was confiscated, especially money. They spoke freely, they said what they thought, and they didn't expect to be treated the way they were treated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the event in Pakrac, and this is the last thing I want to ask you, you mentioned that the JNA came there and the situation calmed down. Were there at the same time also politicians from the federal level coming to Pakrac and negotiating peace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The politicians from the federal level I think at that time Mesic came, but I don't remember anyone else coming other than those four deputy ministers for internal affairs. I don't know about any others.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are the questions that I have to raise. I wonder if I should now also address briefly the two documents, how we got them and what we intend to do. But the witness would actually not be necessarily be present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The only question is a question of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I can do that very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to the document tab 7, it is not the Prosecution's position that these are official minutes from this meeting. The Prosecution believes that this is a report about this meeting, actually produced by this person mentioned in the last line of the document, and the Prosecution will -- we don't have this person on the witness list, and also not another participant in this meeting, because we thought that this witness would actually confirm that this was the content of the meeting. We would have to add these two persons to our witness list. One a participant and then the person we believe made this draft. And we received this document from the Croatian authorities. And in relation to this other document, C-2768, this is also a document that we received from the Croatian government, and the purpose to put it to the witness was actually only that he confirms certain contents in this document, not to authenticate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. It remains to exhibit the witness statement, the statement, date of interview, 1st to the 4th of May. Is that the relevant statement, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll get a number, Prosecution Exhibit number, for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, and it has to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecutor's Exhibit 332, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness C-037, that concludes your evidence. I'm sorry you've been kept so long, but thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are, of course, free to go. The case will be adjourned until Monday morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of October 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
